name: Radioactive decay, nuclear equations and half-life

terms.definition: An unstable nucleus gives out radiation to become more stable; it is random.
terms.examiner: You cannot predict which nucleus decays next.

terms.definition: The rate at which a source of unstable nuclei decays, measured in becquerels (Bq).
Two protons and two neutrons (a helium nucleus); stopped by paper or a few cm of air; strongly ionising.
terms.examiner: Mass number falls by 4, atomic number by 2.

terms.definition: A high-speed electron ejected from the nucleus as a neutron turns into a proton; stopped by a few mm of aluminium.
terms.examiner: Atomic number rises by 1; mass number unchanged.

terms.definition: Electromagnetic radiation from the nucleus; very penetrating, weakly ionising.
terms.examiner: No change in the nucleus's mass or charge.

terms.definition: The time it takes for the number of nuclei in a sample to halve, or for the count rate to fall to half.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: express the net decline as a ratio.
